scope: Corollary 7.1 (Thin and cheap rounding of fractional cuts) of the manuscript “A polynomial-time construction of strong thin trees” (preprints/A-polynomial-time-construction-of-strong-thin-trees-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 174 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 da0e75ba53ff393f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix once and for all an integer B ≥ max{1, C}, where C is the constant in Theorem 1.1. Let G = (V, E) be a finite undirected graph on n ≥ 2 vertices, given by an explicit list of edge records; in this corollary, loops and parallel records are allowed. Given nonnegative rational numbers xe, ce in binary, suppose that x(δG(S)) := X e∈δG(S) xe ≥ 1 (∅ ̸= S ⊊ V ). There is a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the total binary input length, that returns a spanning tree T ⊆ {e ∈ E : xe > 0} satisfying simultaneously |δT (S)| ≤ 24B x(δG(S)) (∅ ̸= S ⊊ V ), (7.1) c(T) := X e∈T ce ≤ 24B X e∈E cexe. (7.2) The cut inequalities are a promise on the input; no metric assumption on the costs is required.
